10.1002_adfm.202528551: The film‐forming uniformity and charge extraction capability of cathode interlayers (CILs) are critical to the performance of organic photovoltaic (OPV) modules, yet CILs scalable to module fabrication remain underexplored. Herein, we design four naphthalimide‐based CILs by independently varying the π ‐bridges (furan or thiophene) and the terminal groups (amine or imidazole), denoted as F‐NN, T‐NN, F‐M, and T‐M, via a facile two‐step synthetic procedure free of column purification. We find that two imidazole‐terminated naphthalimides (F‐M and T‐M) allow more favorable cathode work function tuning and adopt unified molecular orientations, which collectively improve charge extraction and film‐forming uniformity of CILs. Consequently, small‐area OPVs based on F‐M and T‐M deliver power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) of 19.35% and 19.49%, respectively. More importantly, the same molecular alignments in CILs mitigate defect formation during scale‐up, resulting prominent PCEs of 16.70% and 16.26% for the F‐M and T‐M based modules with an aperture area of 20.25 cm 2 , respectively, outperforming the amine‐terminated naphthalimides (F‐NN and T‐NN) based counterparts. These results highlight orientation control, via imidazole terminals, as a feasible route to high‐efficiency OPV modules and offer guidance for future CIL design.
10.1007_s00604-025-07669-x: α-Fe 2 O 3 nanoparticles possess a narrow band gap (~2.1 eV) and exhibit strong absorption in the visible light range, making them promising candidates for photocatalytic applications. However, their poor electrical conductivity, high electron–hole recombination rate, and short charge diffusion length limit their practical performance. To address these limitations, α-Fe 2 O 3 was integrated with Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene to construct a composite photo-Fenton catalyst that drives RAFT polymerization. In this system, the MXene substrate not only disperses α-Fe 2 O 3 nanoparticles efficiently but also facilitates the generation of abundant photoinduced electrons under visible-light excitation. This enhances the Fe 3+ /Fe 2+ redox cycling and accelerates H 2 O 2 decomposition, yielding a high concentration of hydroxyl radicals (•OH). To further explore the functional applicability of this catalyst, it was employed in a biosensing platform for the ultrasensitive detection of microRNA-144. In this design, the •OH radicals initiate RAFT polymerization, allowing for a significant amplification of the electrochemical signal. The resulting sensor exhibits a wide detection range (0.01 fM to 10 pM) and an ultralow detection limit of 4.44 aM. These findings highlight the potential of α-Fe 2 O 3 /Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene composites in photocatalysis, polymer chemistry, and biomedical sensing, offering new insights for future technological innovations.
10.1016_j.ijdrr.2026.106375: : Flood emergencies place severe strain on urban transport systems, particularly when evacuation depends on organised transport rather than private vehicles, as is the case for many transit-dependent groups such as older people, individuals with disabilities, and residents of care facilities. Planning under these conditions is challenging because road networks are often disrupted, congestion is highly uncertain, and warning times can be limited. This paper proposes an integrated transit-based evacuation planning framework that combines agent-based traffic simulation with scenario-based stochastic optimisation to support decision-making under such uncertainty. The framework uses simulation to generate realistic, congestion-aware travel times under different flood scenarios and embeds these directly into a stochastic mixed-integer optimisation model that accounts for shared transport resources, receiving centre capacities, and evacuation time windows. To ensure the approach remains computationally practical, a logic-based Benders decomposition solution method is developed and compared with a monolithic formulation. The framework is demonstrated through a case study in a flood-prone regional area of Australia, showing that it can produce feasible and robust evacuation plans while substantially improving solution stability and runtime performance. The results also highlight the strong influence of evacuation time windows and inter-facility collaboration on evacuation outcomes. Overall, the study offers a practical and scalable decision-support approach for improving the planning of transit-based evacuations in flood-prone communities.
10.1021_acsami.6c13949: Reprogramming the transport preference of crystalline membranes offers a useful strategy for adapting a single membrane platform to different gas-separation tasks. Herein, we report ionic liquid (IL) engineering of pure ZIF-8 membranes to switch H2/CO2 transport from H2- to CO2-preferential behavior. A continuous ZIF-8 membrane was first fabricated on an anodic aluminum oxide support by cathodic deposition, followed by the loading of an IL of type 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium bis(trifluoromethylsulfonyl)imide ([BMIM][TFSI]). The compact, well-intergrown, and crystalline ZIF-8 membrane was preserved after IL incorporation, and vibrational spectroscopy provided evidence for molecular interactions between confined [BMIM][TFSI] and the ZIF-8 framework. Gas-permeation measurements revealed that increasing IL loading decreased both H2 and CO2 permeances, indicating an increased transport resistance caused by partial pore occupation. However, the H2 permeance decreased significantly more rapidly than the CO2 permeance. The H2/CO2 selectivity decreased from 3.6 for the pristine ZIF-8 membrane to approximately 0.3 at 15 vol % ionic-liquid loading, corresponding to a CO2/H2 selectivity close to 3. The separation reversal originates from the combined effects of IL-induced pore narrowing and preferential CO2 affinity. This work demonstrates that confined ILs can reprogram adsorption-diffusion coupling in MOF membranes and provides a route toward process-adaptive gas-separation membranes.
